builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Do Verifier Judgments Survive Abstraction? Measuring Verification Transport for LLM Agent Evaluation
summary: The method replaces single-view, native-representation verifier accuracy measurement with a matched-view reliability test that checks whether the same verifier's judgments survive abstraction, delegation, and history compaction, plus the practice of attaching execution provenance to abstracted views. Cost is modest engineering overhead: constructing or logging provenance-bearing views of each execution and re-running the verifier per view, which adds verifier API or inference calls roughly proportional to the number of views tested. What can fail is that provenance recovery degrades when provenance is lossy or unavailable, low transport failure can mask over-abstention by evidence-grounded protocols rather than true correctness, and results on four benchmarks may not transfer to domain-specific agent traces.
rationale: The reader already operates LLM verifiers through APIs on a single GPU budget, and this is a low-cost evaluation-hardening practice (logging provenance and re-verifying across views) that directly exposes a measured failure mode in production agent pipelines.
technique: Verification transport testing for agent verifiers

claims.statement: The method replaces single-view, native-representation verifier accuracy measurement with a matched-view reliability test that checks whether the same verifier's judgments survive abstraction, delegation, and history compaction, plus the practice of attaching execution provenance to abstracted views. Cost is modest engineering overhead: constructing or logging provenance-bearing views of each execution and re-running the verifier per view, which adds verifier API or inference calls roughly proportional to the number of views tested. What can fail is that provenance recovery degrades when provenance is lossy or unavailable, low transport failure can mask over-abstention by evidence-grounded protocols rather than true correctness, and results on four benchmarks may not transfer to domain-specific agent traces.
Across four benchmarks and seven verifier backbones, up to ~31% of verifier judgments fail under macro abstraction and delegation; restoring execution provenance recovers 85.5% of these failures.
